div.head: Episc 6
div.ab: Ne seall he geþafian ænig unfiht ne who gemet ne fals gewihte; ac hit gebyreð, þæt [b]e his ræde fare ⁊ be his gewitnesse ægwhylc lahriht, ge burhriht ge landriht; ⁊ ælc burhgemet ⁊ He sceall æt tihtlan ladunge gedihtan, þæt ænig man oðrum ænig who beodan ne mæge aðor oððe on aþe on ordale.lc wægpundern be be his dihte gescift swiðe riht, þe læs ænig man oðrum misbeode ⁊ ðurh pæt syngige ealles to swyþe.

He must not permit any injustice, not an incorrect measurement nor a false weight; but it is proper that every law – both law in the town and law in the country – undergo his review and consent. And every town measurement and every weigh-scale is to be properly adjusted under his supervision, lest any man defraud another and thereby sin all too greatly.

Non debet pati (Nec p.d.) aliquod iniustum uel (aliquam circomuentionem) iniuste mensure uel iniusti ponderis; sed conuenit, ut per consilium et testimonium eius omne legis rectum (scitum) et burgi mensura et omne pondus (ponderis) sit secundum dictionem eius institutum ualde rectum, ne quis alium (proximum suum) seducat et^per hoc (pro quo) decidat in peccatum.
